title: Verdant Ceramics
summary: A tactile identity for a small-batch ceramics studio, shaped by the forms of their glazes.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.text: Verdant makes small runs of tableware by hand. They needed an identity that felt as considered as their pieces, without competing with them.

sections.heading: The approach
sections.text: We traced the silhouettes of thirty pieces and reduced them to a family of soft forms. These became the logo mark, packaging die-lines and a set of stamps used directly on kraft boxes.

sections.heading: The outcome
sections.text: A calm, flexible system the studio applies themselves — from shelf labels to their online shop — with no designer needed for everyday work.

title: Field & Folio
summary: Layout and type system for an independent quarterly on craft and slow living.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.text: A new print quarterly wanted a design system its two-person team could use issue after issue.

sections.heading: The approach
sections.text: A strict three-column grid, a serif for reading and one expressive display face, with room for photography to breathe. Every spread was tested at print size.

sections.heading: The outcome
sections.text: Four issues produced on the system so far, each with its own character but an unmistakable shared voice.

title: Seedling Series
summary: Fifty days of abstract botanical drawings, later released as a limited print set.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.text: One drawing a day for fifty days, using only three shapes: a curve, a seed and a line.

sections.heading: The process
sections.text: The constraint pushed each drawing toward abstraction. Halfway through, the forms stopped looking like plants and started looking like a language.

sections.heading: The result
sections.text: A series of twelve risograph prints and the vector library now sold in the shop as the Organic Shapes Library.

title: Nocturne
summary: Interface and design system for a sleep and wind-down app that avoids screen glare.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.text: Nocturne helps people wind down in the evening. Its interface needed to be calm, legible in the dark and free of attention tricks.

sections.heading: The approach
sections.text: A warm, low-contrast night palette tuned for accessibility, slow transitions and a type scale that stays readable at low brightness.

sections.heading: The outcome
sections.text: A design system of 60 components and a measurable increase in evening session completion.

title: Atelier Moss
summary: Identity and website for an interior architecture practice working with natural materials.

sections.heading: The brief
sections.text: A young practice needed a presence as quiet and material as their interiors.

sections.heading: The approach
sections.text: An understated wordmark, a palette sampled from stone, oak and linen, and a website built around large photography and short, honest writing.

sections.heading: The outcome
sections.text: A brand that wins the right clients: most enquiries now mention the website by name.

title: Almanac Essays
summary: A self-published essay collection, designed and typeset from cover to colophon.

sections.heading: The idea
sections.text: Collect a year of newsletter essays into one object worth keeping.

sections.heading: The process
sections.text: Writing, editing, typesetting and cover design done in one place, so every decision served the reading experience.

sections.heading: The result
sections.text: A small first run that sold out, and the foundation for The Quiet Studio ebook.
